text:
Noah W: quick sync - proposal: let router-local agents make emergency fallback decisions but require a signed "guardrail" bundle from control plane that limits actions. thoughts?
Ivy T: love that. makes local fast-path safe. what fields in the guardrail bundle?
Rahul P: minimal set: policy_id, allowed_fallback_ids, tenant_cohorts, max_flip_rate, ttl, signature_kid. keep it tiny.
Noah W: exactly. agent verifies signature and enforces max_flip_rate (e.g., 3 flips / 10m). if exceeded, agent goes passive and notifies control plane.
Ivy T: how to handle stale guardrails if agent is offline beyond ttl? safest is passive-only until it re-syncs.
Rahul P: agree. also add dry-run flag so we can roll out and observe decisions without affecting traffic.
SRE Bot: note: instrument judger.decision and judger.flip_count metrics and include policy_id in traces.
Noah W: KV-warmup note: switching models may cold-start KV cache. agent should emit fallback_cost estimate and we should document expected token-latency penalty.
Ivy T: revocation path: control plane pushes revocation via fanout channel and PRL pulled by agents every 5s. add audit log with operator id + incident id.
Rahul P: security: store signing private keys in HSM, rotate weekly, edges only need public KID/thumbprint.
Noah W: ops runbook snippet: passive -> emergency -> auto phases. emergency requires notification to #oncall and a short-lived safe-policy tombstone if revoke happens.
DeployBot: guardrail v0.1 pushed to 8/8 edge agents at 1788881260
Ivy T: action items: Rahul to spec guardrail proto; Noah to add metrics; i'll add dry-run controls to rollout UI.
Noah W: thanks, small local decision surface + control-plane authority should give us fast SLO-safe fallbacks.
